comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 catalogue specifies 180 EC for the regular full-time Philosophy degree. The third year includes 42 EC free choice, a 6 EC specialisation course linked to the thesis group and the 12 EC thesis.
components: Choose an approved philosophy elective or an additional specialisation course.
Up to 12 EC may come from first-year courses. Choices may include a minor, internship or study abroad.
Take the course linked to the chosen thesis group before starting the thesis.
Complete year one, Text, Context and Debate and 12 EC of specialisation courses. Take the linked thesis specialisation course.

core: History of philosophy across ancient, medieval, modern and contemporary traditions
Ethics, value theory, justice, political and social philosophy
Metaphysics, epistemology, perception, language, cognition and reality
Formal logic, argument analysis, critical thinking and the linguistic turn
Philosophy of science, scientific evidence and relations among philosophy, science and technology
Close reading, philosophical writing, research methods and independent thesis work
adjacent: Ethics and politics as a coherent direction in justice, institutions and moral judgment
Mind, language and world as a coherent direction in cognition, perception, knowledge and reality
Comparative and global philosophy across Chinese, Indian, Islamic and intercultural traditions
questions: What justice requires and how moral and political institutions should be assessed
Whether perception and reason give reliable knowledge of reality
What distinguishes scientific knowledge and evidence from other forms of knowledge
How philosophical ideas shape identity, culture and society

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

alternatives.label: Philosophy, Argument and Intellectual History
alternatives.concept: Study major questions about ethics, mind, freedom and political life. Develop formal reasoning and argument alongside historical, literary and cultural interpretation.
alternatives.labelReason: Introductory philosophy and rhetoric support ethics, philosophy of mind and formal logic. Historical and literary methods provide context for advanced study of agency, emotion, argument and interpretation.
progression: Introductory philosophy and rhetoric support ethics, philosophy of mind and formal logic. Historical and literary methods provide context for advanced study of agency, emotion, argument and interpretation.

alternatives.label: Ethics, Politics, Justice and Institutions
alternatives.concept: Study how people justify laws, institutions and political decisions. Connect moral and political philosophy with rights, justice, legal reasoning and social movements.
alternatives.labelReason: The law gateway precedes constitutional, European Union and criminal law. Ethics and political philosophy provide concepts for evaluating rights and institutions. Social theory and historical research extend the study of justice.
alternatives.distinctness: Gives greater weight to law, institutions and social justice than to literary and historical interpretation or cognition.
progression: The law gateway precedes constitutional, European Union and criminal law. Ethics and political philosophy provide concepts for evaluating rights and institutions. Social theory and historical research extend the study of justice.

alternatives.label: Mind, Language and Cognition
alternatives.concept: Study how minds perceive, think and use language. Combine philosophy of mind and agency with logic, cognitive science, language analysis and computational approaches.
alternatives.labelReason: The brain and behaviour gateway precedes psycholinguistics and cognitive neuroscience. Philosophy of mind and logic support advanced work on agency and perception. Statistics supports evidence synthesis, and programming prepares for machine learning.
alternatives.distinctness: Gives greater weight to language, cognitive science and empirical methods than to law or historical interpretation.
progression: The brain and behaviour gateway precedes psycholinguistics and cognitive neuroscience. Philosophy of mind and logic support advanced work on agency and perception. Statistics supports evidence synthesis, and programming prepares for machine learning.

selection.assessment: The broad option connects central philosophy, argument and intellectual history. The additional options develop justice and institutions or mind and language. Cross-cultural and scientific themes are present through related courses. UCR has narrower coverage of non-Western philosophy and lacks a dedicated philosophy-of-science sequence.

notes.text: UvA has dedicated sequences in practical and theoretical philosophy, philosophy of science and philosophical research, plus a required thesis. The UCR options combine philosophy with related disciplines. Their coverage of philosophy of science and non-Western philosophy is more limited.

audience.programmeDescription: Philosophy at the University of Amsterdam is taught in Dutch. The programme develops philosophical argument, logic, historical interpretation and independent research. Students choose specialist courses and write a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines philosophy and logic with history and literature. Two further options focus on justice and institutions or on mind, language and cognition. UvA offers more specialist philosophy courses.
